summary: Tenant cookie namespace collision causes silent diversion to fallback variant during canary rollout
description: Issue summary: Several Luminous Health tenants in eu-west started receiving responses from the degraded fallback variant during a scheduled canary rollout. Impact: ~3% of requests for the account were routed to fallback variant causing degraded quality and increased costs. Environment: production (eu-west), hosted API fronted by edge-proxy and route-mapper. Observed window: 2026-03-11 02:10 - 2026-03-11 04:25 UTC. Customers reported mixed model outputs and one billing spike alert. Initial hypothesis: fallback logic triggered by health signals. Final cause: collision between tenant sticky cookie name namespace and a new canary cookie suffix introduced by route-mapper; hash-salt mismatch caused route lookup to resolve to an older shard that only had fallback variants active for a short window.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a long-lived session cookie name 'rwd_session_<tenant_id>' set by edge-proxy
2) Simulate canary by toggling canary flag for route in route-mapper (weight 10%)
3) Edge-proxy appends suffix '-canary' for per-cohort stickiness creating 'rwd_session_<tenant_id>-canary' in some code paths
4) If a request arrives with legacy cookie (no suffix) but the route-mapper hash-salt was rolled with suffix-aware hashing, the lookup falls back to shard that had fallback active
5) Observe mixed routing to degraded variant for requests with mismatched cookie forms
logs: [route-mapper] 2026-03-11T02:12:06Z WARN hash mismatch tenant=LH-231 cookie_name="rwd_session_LH-231" computed_slot=93 expected_slot=157 falling_back=true
[serving-runtime] 2026-03-11T02:12:07Z INFO request routed tenant=LH-231 model=redwood/llama-2-13b variant=fallback node=dedicated-34
investigation_notes: 03/11 03:00 - Support triaged with customer: pattern limited to Luminous Health; they use a proxy that also manipulates cookies (internal middleware).
03/11 03:20 - SRE examined route-mapper release notes and found commit that added suffix-aware cookie hashing to support scoped canary cookies (PR #412).
03/11 03:30 - Replayed requests from request-logs; reproducer showed cookie name canonicalization mismatch between edge-proxy (older instances) and new route-mapper hashing logic.

Observed that when cookie form differs (with or without '-canary' suffix) the hash function used by route-mapper returned different shard ids and those shards briefly had fallback-only traffic during canary ramp down.
Hypothesis validated: collision occurs when upstream middleware rewrites cookie names for a subset of tenant sessions while route-mapper expects a different canonical cookie name.
comments: Aisha Kapoor (Support) 2026-03-11 03:05 UTC: Customer reports ~3% degraded responses, provided example request ids: req-48213, req-48285. Confirmed incident window and asked for logs. Escalating to SRE.
Diego Morales (SRE) 2026-03-11 03:22 UTC: Noted recent route-mapper change to suffix-aware hashing (PR #412). Collecting edge and route-mapper instances to correlate cookie forms.

Marta Lin (Customer Engineering) 2026-03-11 04:00 UTC: Luminous Health confirmed they have an authentication middleware that appends '-canary' to session cookie for some sessions — this was not previously common knowledge.
Diego Morales (SRE) 2026-03-11 05:14 UTC: Hotfix deployed to route-mapper in eu-west: compatibility mode enabled to ignore suffix when computing tenant hash. Monitoring metrics now.
Aisha Kapoor (Support) 2026-03-11 06:00 UTC: Customer confirmed quality returned to baseline. Temporary mitigation: route-mapper compatibility mode. Scheduling follow-up for permanent fix.

Diego Morales (SRE) 2026-03-12 10:11 UTC: Rolled permanent fix (route-mapper v1.8.3) that namespaces cookies per-tenant explicitly and adds deterministic canonicalization. Also deployed edge-proxy validation to log unexpected cookie names for 72h.
Customer (Luminous Health - PM) 2026-03-12 15:34 UTC: Appreciative of fast response; requested a short postmortem and a config option to opt-in to suffix-aware behavior in future rollouts.
resolution: Root cause: Cookie namespace collision caused inconsistent tenant hashing between edge-proxy instances and the new suffix-aware route-mapper, resulting in misrouted requests to shards with fallback-only variants during a canary window.
Immediate mitigation: Enabled route-mapper compatibility mode in eu-west to canonicalize cookie names (ignore '-canary' suffix) and rolled back suffix-only hashing for affected shards.

Fix deployed: route-mapper v1.8.3 — explicit per-tenant cookie namespace mapping and canonicalizer; edge-proxy updated to log unexpected cookie forms for visibility (github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/877).

Customer mitigation: We issued Set-Cookie Max-Age=0 for legacy cookie name via edge to clear stale cookies for the tenant; recommended Luminous Health remove client middleware that appends suffix or coordinate with us for an opt-in canary header.
- Engineering: Add automated preflight check in canary rollout pipeline to detect cookie name collisions (owner: Diego) — due 2026-03-25.
- Product/Docs: Document cookie namespace best practices in public docs and enterprise onboarding flow (owner: Marta) — due 2026-03-19.
- CS: Offer customer a configuration toggle to opt-in for suffix-aware canaries and assist with migration (owner: Aisha) — scheduled meeting 2026-03-16.
Incident closed after 48h monitoring with no recurrence reported.
